rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.text:
People struggle with old photos they only vaguely remember. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Among these, many stories say search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos: 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Others say the photo was already gone: 20 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Some say the photo was in the results but hard to spot among similar ones: 9 of 115 stories (8%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] One post sums up the hunt as “looking through old photos” [[story|bab90b1de62ccbe1ae30a49d63fb19f823c1c5c8:0]]. One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown by why people kept the photo?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What kinds of details do people actually remember about a photo when trying to find it (what they recall vs what they forgot or were wrong about)?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot reliably tell what people remember, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]][[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]  
People most often remembered what was in the photo: 47 of 115 stories (41%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
Some also remembered when it was taken: 24 of 115 stories (21%). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
Fewer remembered who was in it: 14 of 115 stories (12%), or where it was taken: 11 of 115 stories (10%). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:who:core]][[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:where:core]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
One person wrote they had to “scroll through … to find one from 2019” [[story|1233de10dc517a78f662c1618c4d4f5e5ccbc658:0]].  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick view of what people forget, side by side with what they remember?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What information (types of cues or details) did people report they had forgotten about the photo they were trying to find?
rows.text:
People often forgot the date or year of the photo they wanted. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
Some forgot the exact place or the venue name. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
A few did not remember if it was a photo, a video, or a screenshot. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
A few also forgot which app or account it was in. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
One person said they had “totally forgotten” old screenshots they found — “I had totally forgotten about” [[story|b526179286c2b3c9db1c198db44e50543ed2f275:0]].  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Do you want a quick recap that uses just those four kinds of missing info?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.text:
People often type a simple word they do remember, like an object, action, or text seen in the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] They sometimes search by a few vivid details together, like “daughter,” “panda,” and “yellow raincoat.” [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[story|247694a905c13ced6a041728c4685f9c02dcbd78:0]] Others try one clear word for the thing they recall, such as “bicycle.” [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]] Some describe an action they remember, like “vomit,” though the search may not match it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples grouped by what people remembered (object, text, action)?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.text:
Often, yes. In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] In 38 of 115 stories (33%), nothing went wrong — they found the photo — so the search can work. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] One person wrote “I can’t find them on back up Google photos” [[story|912c6cc3068a194559168f5b66e2dbc5bc867dc8:0]], which fits stories where the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to see examples of the clues people tried?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: The stories do not contain any financial data, so they cannot tell us Google Photos’ annual revenue. These are public posts about trying to find a photo, not company financial reports. They cannot answer this, and only audited financial statements or official disclosures could.

rows.question: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.restated: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
These are public posts about trying to find a photo. They cannot tell us monthly active users, success or failure rates, or any absolute user counts. This question needs usage telemetry or official reports from the product team, not stories.

Data that could answer it would be audited product analytics or a published MAU figure from the company.

rows.question: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.restated: What proportion of searches that start from vague or imprecise memories succeed in finding the target photo?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: The stories cannot give any success rate for searches from vague memories. They are public posts about trying to find a photo, not usage data that measures outcomes across all searches or users. They also do not track attempts that people didn’t post. To answer your question, we would need comprehensive usage logs that record all vague-memory searches and whether a photo was found, linked to a defined user or query base.

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.gap: the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split
rows.text:
The stories do not reliably record Android or iPhone, so they cannot say who struggles more. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

What they can say is how often posts mention who was using the phone at all: 91 of 115 stories say anything about whose phone, and who was doing the searching. [[analysis_coverage|1.6]]

They also show what people remember and try: 192 of 331 stories say anything about what they actually remember about the photo. [[analysis_coverage|2.1]]

One person wrote “No matter what device I try the search function on, it only shows me a few photos.” [[story|c6af9dfa5d9eb9733869f6f5824fc1c29a4acbae:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Do you want a breakdown by what people remembered versus how they searched?*

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Is Google Photos search quality worse now than it was before Ask Photos launched?
rows.gap: the stories were not compared across time, so there is no before-and-after
rows.text:
Search quality has not been shown to change since Ask Photos launched; the stories have no time-series or before/after markers tied to that event. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]  
We can say only what people described in public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]  
Only 46 of 331 stories say anything about what search showed them. [[analysis_coverage|5.6]]  
One Reddit post says “I am not seeing great search results with Ask Photos” and finds fewer sunsets than expected. [[story|b4a4d8c14233f96a727cec35a5c67f19ad91d59a:1]]  
Another Reddit post says “It used to find all images … Now it can’t even find the most simple and blatant keywords.” [[story|9a7306c83836251e47a6ca073afd34441115de00:0]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick read on what kinds of search words people said did not work?*

rows.question: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.restated: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.gap: the stories do not compare how well other photo apps search
rows.draft:
These stories cannot show whether Apple Photos search is better than Google Photos search. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

People posted 31,235 public comments, and 314 posts were about trying to find a photo, giving 331 stories told by 316 people. [[analysis_funnel|collected]][[analysis_funnel|kept]][[analysis_funnel|stories]]
Only 31 of 331 stories say what search showed, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_coverage|5.6]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
91 of 115 stories say whose phone and who searched, but they do not compare other photo apps. [[analysis_coverage|1.6]][[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]
One person said “text search Apple photos … disappointed” and “text search Google photos and instantly find the image I want.” [[story|b7113e3689e0674b9cd8b089fb3bcd093e40d3eb:0]]

*Want a closer look at what people tried inside Google Photos?*
rows.text:
The stories cannot tell you all of this: the stories do not compare how well other photo apps search. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

rows.question: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.restated: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.gap: few public posts say anything about how far down the results they went — 2 of 115 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users
rows.text:
Very few posts say how far people went before deciding. [[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]]  
Among stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, 1 of 115 stories (1%) say they went a few scrolls. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
Another 1 of 115 stories (1%) say they went all the way down. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
Only 2 of 115 stories say anything about how far down the results they went. [[analysis_coverage|6.6]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to see how this differs when people searched versus just scrolled?*

rows.question: How many attempts do people make before they give up?

rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on how long they kept trying to rely on it
rows.draft:
These stories cannot tell a firm number of tries, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on how long people kept trying. [[analysis_reliability|q:8.1]][[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]  
Most stories that say anything report one try: 21 of 115 stories (18%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_coverage|8.1]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]]  
Some describe a few tries over minutes: 6 of 115 stories (5%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:_all]]  
A small group reached an hour or more: 3 of 115 stories (3%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=hour_or_more@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
“One try” also shows up in 8 of 48 stories (17%) for photos whose post does not say why they were kept — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

rows.text:

rows.question: And how does that split by kind of photo?
rows.restated: Which step does finding the photo first go wrong in, broken down by kind of photo (sentimental, practical, both, unclear)?

rows.question: Does that differ for utility photos?
rows.restated: Do people searching for practical photos differ in what they type into search first compared with other photo types?

rows.draft:
It partly differs. For utility photos, people often start with a single word, like a code or label. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:utility]] For some, they begin with several keywords. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:utility]] One post shows this style: “I put in ‘VIN’” [[story|33dd763b1d8fb1aac1afd0a4f6fcb1cec82b40ef:0]] For memory photos, a single word is also common in 11 of 48 stories (23%) — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:sentimental]] Across all vaguely remembered photos, single words show up in 19 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.text:
The stories cannot tell you all of this: only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes) — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

- In 8 of 21 stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, among photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes), the first thing that went wrong was that the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|33dd763b1d8fb1aac1afd0a4f6fcb1cec82b40ef:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.restated: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.text:
People often say the search does not understand plain words like “receipt,” so nothing shows up. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One person wrote, “I couldn't find the receipt for my laptop, 'receipt' returned nothing.” [[story|probe-inj-04]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Others say the search brings back many wrong photos when they try related words like “scrap.” [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One post said it “returned way too many images of my shop.” [[story|0ef3821f2d59998617a4b53f428fd49c9a22d2ff:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.text:
Many stories say the search shows the wrong photos or misses what people type. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] People also find the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]] Some people never use the search box; they just scroll or look elsewhere. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:_all]] One person said “'dog park' never finds the photo of my dog at the park in winter.” [[story|probe-inj-06]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One limit is that these are public posts, not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
